subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep log-only fallback once OAuth inheritance is live-proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and repository policy treats fallback behavior and auth/provider routing as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and fail-closed or visible warning
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define an operator-visible or fail-closed behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split fallback visibility after proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation portion after live proof and track fallback visibility or route-loss warning as a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Accept log-only fallback
options.body: Maintain the existing logged fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and fail-closed or visible warning
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define an operator-visible or fail-closed behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history across OpenAI identity, auth-profile storage, Codex app-server state, and session/subagent routing.
